messages:
Anya: quick postmortem — after yesterday's canary we saw slot saturation in dedicated pools. root cause: SLO/penalty normalization got accidentally moved from policy compiler to runtime during the 'adapter-slimline' refactor, so compiler-generated route weights were being re-normalized per-decision. that made hedged routes disproportionately favored for certain tenants.
Mike: ugh. can you paste the smallest repro? the logs I saw showed a lot of repeated compatibility runs for the same request id.
Anya: simplest repro is a tenant with tier=gold + region-preference EU and a mix of cost-limited + latency-bound routes. compiler used weight vector [0.2,0.5,0.3] and expected runtime to respect relative ratios. runtime re-normalized with dynamic penalty spikes so effective weight became ~[0.1,0.7,0.2].
Chris: suggests: keep invariant normalization inside the compiler step. runtime can apply additive penalties (delta) but should only scale via a single monotonic factor, never re-normalize the original weight vector. that keeps compiler intent stable.
Mike: agree. moving normalization back to compiler seems low-risk. what's the compatibility matrix for older clients / adapters? any adapters that expect runtime normalization?
Anya: we found one legacy adapter (route-compat v1) that assumed runtime would clamp and re-normalize; it's ~1% of traffic. plan: shim for v1 that exposes "compat_nominal" field and opt into runtime-clamp for that adapter only.
Julia: migration checklist: 1) revert refactor commit with unit tests 2) add explicit invariant test that compiler outputs normalized weights and runtime only applies an additive penalty/hysteresis 3) add telemetry: reported fields (compiler_weights, runtime_penalty_vector, final_weights) 4) rollout canary to 1% then 10% then 100% over 24h with watch on p95 latency, GPU queue length, and hedged-success-rate.
Chris: also propose a small API/contract change to make the boundary explicit: compiler emits "base_weights" + "normalization_kind":"absolute" and runtime accepts only {additive_penalty, multiplier} and must not perform full re-normalize. that will catch regressions.
Mike: any perf impacts? moving normalization to compiler reduces per-decision work but increases metadata size on route blob. how much?
Anya: metadata grows ~120 bytes per route (base_weights + kind). negligible compared to existing route blob (~2.4kb). perf better: runtime avoids sorting/normalizing in hot path.
sre-bot: incident:INC-2026-118 created (link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2026-118) — assigned to @Anya, severity 3.
Julia: tests: add a litmus test for overhang cases where dynamic penalty spikes occur (simulate geo probe suddenly penalizing EU). expected behaviour: final_weights should move proportionally but not flip dominance unless penalty delta > threshold. include a golden set and assert <=10% deviation in non-extreme cases.
Chris: follow-up: create a lint rule in policy-compiler that fails build if it emits fields that allow runtime full-normalize. we can enforce using CI. also add a quick fuzz harness targeting corner weight vectors (tiny values, zeros, all-equal).
Mike: timeline? revert + tests + canary by EOD tomorrow? canary instrumented with telemetry fields Julia asked for?
Anya: yes. I'll open the PR now, include runtime shim for v1 compatibility. will post PR link here.
Anya: PR: https://git.redwood/repo/policy-compiler/pull/487 (WIP) — contains revert + boundary contract + tests. please review. :folded_hands:
Chris: review in a bit. after merge let's run the sim-suite (route-synthesis-sim) overnight and watch the metric deltas.
Julia: note for release notes: "Fix: stability of route weighting — moved normalization back into compiler to preserve route intent and reduce runtime oscillation". keep customer-facing wording non-technical.
Mike: thx team. small ask: let's add an entry to the architecture changelog summarizing the rationale + future work (policy DSL for explicit runtime signals).
Anya: yep will add changelog item and link to this thread.
